source: Open Food Facts (https://world.openfoodfacts.org/), ODbL. off_india.csv read 1 Oct 2026 (India); off_multi.tsv read 6 Oct 2026 (UK, US, France).
note: text = this script's matcher on English ingredient lists (n = English lists in the group, baby food and supplements out). tag = Open Food Facts' additives_tags (any language; n = products with a list or a tag). intense = the WHO's non-sugar sweeteners (acesulfame K, aspartame, sucralose, saccharin, steviol glycosides, neotame, cyclamate, thaumatin and the rest); polyol = sorbitol, maltitol, xylitol, erythritol, isomalt, mannitol, lactitol. Volunteers fill Open Food Facts, so no country's packs are a random sample. Shares: k of n, pct = 100*k/n.

india_named_diet_zero_sugar_free.name_words: diet, sugar free, zero, no sugar, no added sugar, lite, light, unsweetened, keto (product name, any brand words included)

india_warning_check.note: Open Food Facts has no field for FSSAI's sweetener statements. labels_tags carries one only when a volunteer typed it; the ingredient text carries one only when the volunteer pasted the whole back of the pack. So this is a floor on how many packs print the statement, not a measure of it.

india_text_vs_tag.note: Indian English lists where the matcher finds an intense sweetener, and how many of those Open Food Facts also tagged (additives_tags).
